correctness.rationale: Explicit symmetric half-unit-diagonal threshold energy strictly decreases whenever the binary spin vector differs two steps apart, so periods exceed neither one nor two. A fixed mixed part requires outside-neighbor tie; 0/1/2/3 mixed-part case analysis yields precisely two unanimous states and, if all three part sizes are even, the product of the three central-binomial choices. On a two-cycle each part is unchanged or flips homogeneously; two opposite-flipping groups require equal sizes and |2b-r|<s for the stationary part, while three flipping groups require exactly one uniquely largest size. These cases are exhaustive/disjoint. Formula agreement was checked on 1728 weighted macrostate triples and 376824 explicitly updated labelled microstates.

value.rationale: The general Goles–Olivos period bound leaves natural quantitative recurrent-dynamics questions unresolved. The new closed census identifies which communities can oscillate, the exact labelled freedom of a frozen community, and a sharp equal-part-size versus distinct-part-size transition from exactly one to potentially exponentially many primitive two-cycles; it gives all fixed states and the full Artin–Mazur zeta function for every positive three-part size. These are natural, non-arbitrary invariants of a canonical graph family, not just routine recomputation of a table.
